title: Run an SEO audit, show its value and plan 90 days

say: Run an SEO audit, show its value, and plan 90 days.
This is the video for module four of the SEO course.
An SEO audit is a structured check of how well a site and its Business Profile can be found, understood and chosen. It ends with a list of fixes in order.
First, indexing: is the site verified, the sitemap submitted, and are important pages in Google?

panel.heading: Five parts of an SEO audit

say: Second, technical health: secure HTTPS, mobile layout, page speed, broken links.

panel.heading: Five parts of an SEO audit

say: Third, on-page and content: unique titles, one H1, alt text, and helpful content for each keyword group.

panel.heading: Five parts of an SEO audit

say: Fourth, local presence: a verified profile, the right category, and the same name, address and phone everywhere.

panel.heading: Five parts of an SEO audit

say: Fifth, measurement and links. Always work in this order, because a page Google cannot index gains nothing from a better title.

panel.heading: Five parts of an SEO audit
panel.rule: Work in this order. An early problem makes later fixes useless.

say: Record every issue in one row of a sheet, with evidence, impact, effort and the fix. An issue without evidence is only an opinion.
For example, Blessing audits a furniture workshop's website in Aba for her capstone.

say: Get the owner's agreement in writing first. A WhatsApp message is fine. Ask to be added as a Restricted user in Search Console and as a manager on the Business Profile.
Then test like a customer: search, open the site, and try to send a WhatsApp message.

panel.heading: Do and don't when auditing
left: Ask to be added as a user

say: Never ask for passwords. Look at competitors to explain your advice, never to copy them. Never promise rankings. And show the evidence without blaming anyone.

panel.heading: Do and don't when auditing
left: Ask to be added as a user

say: Owners want to know if SEO is worth it. Google says it usually takes four months to a year to show benefit, so share that early.
For example, Blessing reports to the furniture workshop after three months, using only figures the owner gives her.

say: Analytics shows 64 WhatsApp taps from Google search last month. The owner says about 1 in 8 chats becomes a sale. That is 8 sales. His average order is about 180,000 naira, so about 1,440,000 naira.

say: For example, Funke has about 4 hours a week. In days 1 to 14 she fixes her 5 quick wins from the audit.

panel.heading: Fix first, build second, measure last

say: In days 15 to 45 she builds a topic cluster: one main page, Wedding Cakes in Ibadan, plus three supporting articles that all link to it.

panel.heading: Fix first, build second, measure last

say: In days 46 to 75 she builds a second cluster, and posts on her Business Profile every week.

panel.heading: Fix first, build second, measure last

say: In days 76 to 90 she compares with her baseline and writes her report. Then she plans the next 90 days.

say: To earn your certificate, complete the capstone and score at least 70 percent in the final quiz. Check your capstone against these six items before you submit.

panel.heading: Capstone checklist
items: Keyword map with at least 4 topic groups
Audit sheet covering all five parts

say: To remember. Audit in order, with evidence. Start with quick wins. Show value in calls, chats and naira, using the owner's figures. Promise the work, never a ranking. And plan in 90-day cycles.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Audit in order, with evidence for every issue
Start with high-impact, easy quick wins
